forecast-period.text: A trough over central Australia will weaken and contract into WA as a ridge of high pressure extends across southern SA today. The high pressure system is expected to drift into the Tasman Sea by Tuesday as the trough in WA begins to re-extend over western SA on Tuesday, pushing into the state on Wednesday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible early shower about the southern coast, clearing during the late morning. Chance of a thunderstorm in the far northwest. Maximum temperatures near or slightly below average about the southern agricultural area but above average elsewhere. Southeasterly winds in the south, fresh at times near the coast, tending east to northeasterly in the north.

Mostly dry, with isolated showers and thunderstorms developing in the far west during the late afternoon. Maximum temperatures above to well above average. East to northeasterly winds, fresh in the north.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms in the far west, extending to the Eyre Peninsula and southern coasts in the late evening. Maximum temperatures well above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, fresh in the north at times ahead of southwesterly change extending across the west in the evening.

text.p: Isolated showers and thunderstorms extending across the agricultural areas, North West Pastoral and West Coast, becoming scattered in the far west. Maximum temperatures above average in the south and west, grading to well above above average in the north. Light and variable winds in the south, tending northwest to northeasterly in the north.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Wednesday: Dry in the northeast. Generally less than 2 mm through the pastorals and northern agricultural areas, increasing to 2 to 10 mm about the southern agricultural areas. Isolated falls of 10 to 20 mm are possible about the far west, Lower Eyre Peninsula and Kangaroo Island
